QuestionStmt.S: If $f(1) = 1$, $f'(1) = 3$, then the derivative of $f(f(f(x))) + (f(x))^2$ at $x = 1$ is

Solution.S:
Let $y = f(f(f(x))) + (f(x))^2$.

Differentiate:

$$\frac{dy}{dx} = f'(f(f(x))) \cdot f'(f(x)) \cdot f'(x) + 2f(x) \cdot f'(x)$$

At $x = 1$: $f(1) = 1$, $f'(1) = 3$.

$f(f(1)) = f(1) = 1$, $f'(f(1)) = f'(1) = 3$.

$f(f(f(1))) = f(1) = 1$, $f'(f(f(1))) = f'(1) = 3$.

Thus:

$$\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)_{x=1} = 3 \cdot 3 \cdot 3 + 2 \cdot 1 \cdot 3 = 27 + 6 = 33$$

Hence the correct option is D: 33.
